clue.text: Certain to restrain organised workers in a stitch-up

indicators.note: to restrain something is to hold it within, so one word encloses the other here

parts.note: certain means sure
workers organised into a trade union, abbreviated TU

explanation.surface: Unionised workers kept in check by a rigged arrangement, a political 'stitch-up'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stitch-up' looks like slang for a fix or frame; read literally it is a surgical stitching.
explanation.definitionFit: A suture is the stitching that closes a wound, literally a stitch-up by a surgeon.

clue.text: Semi-slave, endlessly cheeky revolutionary

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so the word runs backwards
without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: fresh means cheeky or impertinent

explanation.surface: A half-enslaved peasant who is endlessly insolent and rebellious.
explanation.definitionFit: A serf was a feudal labourer bound to the land, not quite a slave.

clue.text: Chinese food — something boring, not much good?

parts.note: a trepan is a surgical drill, something that bores holes

indicators.note: not much of the word, just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A Chinese dish dismissed as dull and not very good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' is dull on the surface but means drilling holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Trepang, or sea cucumber, is a delicacy in Chinese cooking.

clue.text: Forces surrounding some fortifications

indicators.note: one word surrounds the other, so it is placed around it

parts.note: rams means forces, as when ramming through
part means some, a portion

explanation.surface: Troops encircling some defensive works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forces' looks like troops but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramparts are defensive walls or embankments around a fort.

clue.text: Most eccentric groups of soldiers in company dealing with communications

indicators.note: placed in the company's letters, so those letters enclose the soldiers

parts.note: BT is British Telecom, the UK telephone company
armies are large groups of soldiers

explanation.surface: A telecoms firm hosting military units, perhaps the oddest corporate arrangement imaginable.
explanation.definitionFit: Barmy is British slang for crazy, so the barmiest are the most crazy or odd.

clue.text: Errant Don, I, with a fiasco for the fans?

indicators.note: errant means straying from the proper path, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A wayward man named Don, along with the speaker, has made a mess of things for the supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: Aficionados are keen enthusiasts or devotees of an activity.

clue.text: Northern city half filled with superior old people

indicators.note: half of the word, its first five letters

parts.note: Manchester is a city in northern England
U means upper class or superior in British usage

explanation.surface: A northern city half full of upper-class elderly residents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filled with' is a link; U as 'upper class' is a British social label.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manchu are an ethnic group from Manchuria who ruled China as the Qing dynasty.

clue.text: Animal occupying English lea collapsing on the ground

indicators.note: occupying means filling a space, so one piece sits inside the other
collapsing means falling apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a pig is an animal

explanation.surface: A pig or similar beast squatting on a crumbling English meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal' tempts as the definition but is the occupant; 'collapsing' gives EAL, and 'occupying' sets the beast inside the English meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Epigeal is a botanical term for growing or living on or just above the soil surface.

clue.text: What's to come of shrubby plant that died after short time?

indicators.note: after places the plant and the rest following the short time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
hebe is an evergreen flowering shrub
yon is an old word for that

explanation.surface: Asking what will become of a shrub that died after a brief while.
explanation.definitionFit: The beyond is the afterlife, the unknown future after death.

clue.text: Like a mansion said to be damp and unhealthy

indicators.note: said signals that the word is spoken aloud and matched by a different spelling

parts.note: a mansion is spacious, i.e. roomy

explanation.surface: A grand house rumoured to be damp and bad for the health.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumy describes watery, catarrhal eyes or air full of rheum, so damp and sickly.

clue.text: VIP's report?

parts.note: an important person is a figurative 'big shot', and a loud report or bang is literally a large sound

explanation.surface: A dignitary's announcement, or the bang such a person might make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' means a bang as well as an account, giving the literal reading of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A big noise is an informal term for an important, influential person.

clue.text: One has ice cream melting? Eat it!

definitions.text: One has ice cream melting? Eat it!

indicators.note: melting things lose their shape, so these letters are reformed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's ice cream is going soft, and the speaker urges them to eat it quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ONE HAS ICE CREAM rearrange to the dish, and the whole clue offers it as something to eat instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni cheese is a baked pasta dish in cheese sauce, a dish to eat.

clue.text: Leader of bloggers is to curse, put out when one's included little-known words?

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so these letters are rearranged
the leader is the first letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lead blogger swears in frustration at being given obscure vocabulary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when ... 's included' just adds the I to the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscurities are things hard to understand or little known, such as recondite words.

clue.text: Criticism coming with IT? I celebrate converting for use with computers

parts.note: a dig is a pointed criticism
to sing is to celebrate in song

explanation.surface: Someone takes flak about their IT skills but rejoices anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitising is turning information into digital data that computers can process.

clue.text: Daughter is put to bed and kept inside, separated

indicators.note: one word is kept inside the other, so it is enclosed

explanation.surface: A daughter is sent to bed and confined indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put to' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Disbanded describes a group broken up, its members separated.

clue.text: Miscellany in large book needing no introduction

indicators.note: lacking an introduction means the word's opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a folio is a large-format book

explanation.surface: An anthology inside a big book that speaks for itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An olio is a hotchpotch or medley, a crossword staple for a mixed collection.

clue.text: Whine and sob terribly — can this bring luck to one of couple?

definitions.text: can this bring luck to one of couple?

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone whining and sobbing awfully, hoping something will bring them luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A wishbone is pulled by two people, and the one with the longer piece gets a wish.

clue.text: Bank in decline with lake drying up

indicators.note: a lake drying up vanishes, so its letter is removed

parts.note: a slide is a decline, as in prices
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A riverbank sloping down beside a lake that is drying out.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank is the side of a river, so side can stand for a bank.

clue.text: Very good stars showing blemishes

parts.note: def is slang for excellent
aces are star performers

explanation.surface: Top stars show their flaws.
explanation.definitionFit: To deface something is to spoil its surface, so defaces means blemishes as a verb.

clue.text: Danced, as repeatedly instructed

parts.note: qua is Latin-derived 'in the capacity of', i.e. as
drilled means trained by repetition

explanation.surface: Someone dances, just as they had been told to over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: To quadrille is to dance the quadrille, a square dance for four couples.

clue.text: More than one wild animal, see, climbs

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning see
rises means climbs

explanation.surface: Look, a group of wild beasts climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorises are slow-moving nocturnal primates, wild animals of Asia.

clue.text: Awful moan that is indicating isolation and anxiety

indicators.note: awful means dreadfully done, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A dreadful groan that reveals loneliness and worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Anomie is a sociological term for alienation from social norms and the unease it brings.

clue.text: Dogs as exceptional sniffers can help, left to go free

indicators.note: exceptional suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged
going free means leaving the mix, so that letter is taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: Dogs with exceptional noses might help out once released.
explanation.walkthrough: Take L from the letters of SNIFFERS CAN HELP and rearrange the rest; 'exceptional' and 'to go free' signal the two steps.
explanation.definitionFit: Affenpinschers are a small terrier-like toy breed with monkeyish faces.

clue.text: European or American in book title

definitions.meaning: Huck ..., the American boy of Mark Twain's Adventures of Huckleberry ...

explanation.surface: A person from one continent or another, named in a book title.
explanation.definitionFit: A Finn comes from Finland; Huckleberry Finn is Twain's Mississippi river hero.

clue.text: Within a month be replaced by six who could lay down law in Rome?

definitions.text: who could lay down law in Rome?

indicators.note: one piece swaps out for another, so the word be gives way to six

parts.note: December is a month
taken as written
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A puzzling instruction: within a month, change things around for six legislators of Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Within' is a link: the swap happens inside the month's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A decemvir was one of ten Roman magistrates appointed to draw up a law code.

clue.text: Dish awful Tories!

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly made, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation dismissing the Conservative party as dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Rösti is a Swiss dish of fried grated potato.

clue.text: Rubbish prize reported in broadcast

parts.note: to dis is to rubbish, i.e. disparage

indicators.note: reported means told aloud, so a word with the same sound is used

parts.note: a purse is prize money, as in a boxing purse

explanation.surface: A dismissive mention of an award made on air.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast seed is to scatter or disperse it widely.

clue.text: One's admiral slain finally at sea

definitions.text: One's admiral slain finally at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are reshuffled
finally picks the last letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Someone's admiral killed at last in a naval battle.
explanation.walkthrough: ONES plus L and N, the last letters of 'admiral' and 'slain', rearrange to the name; the whole clue then describes the man.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Nelson, Britain's most famous admiral, was killed at sea at Trafalgar in 1805.
